summary: Transparent proxy 'CONNECT peek' splits single Range into multipart/byteranges, corrupting presigned shard downloads in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightFrame reports repeated model load failures on their private deployment. The serving nodes intermittently receive corrupted model shard files when fetching presigned S3 shards via VPCE egress. Failure correlates with long-lived model downloads and happens only from behind the customer's corporate egress appliance that performs TLS inspection and HTTP/3-to-HTTP/2 downgrade for deep inspection (appliance reported as 'InspectPro v3.2').

Impact:
- Several serving nodes in us-east-1 failed to startup because shard integrity checks failed (checksum mismatch).
- Production traffic experienced transient 5xx errors as nodes failed to load models and fallback routing kicked in.
- Customer requests SLA credit and assistance to mitigate immediately.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Redwood Private in customer's VPC with VPCE egress through corporate appliance (InspectPro v3.2) configured for TLS inspection and HTTP/3 inspection mode.
2) Pin a large model (gpt-j-6b) and trigger a cold start so serving nodes download sharded model artifacts via presigned S3 URLs.
3) Observe artifact downloader logs and checksums for shard files; correlate with appliance logs that show HTTP/3->HTTP/2 downgrade and a 'CONNECT peek' action.
4) Reproduce by issuing a curl request from a host behind the appliance to the presigned URL with a single Range header; check response headers and body.
5) When issue present, server returns multipart/byteranges (206 with boundary) instead of single 206 and downloader reassembly yields corrupted shard file.
logs: Serving node log excerpt: artifact-downloader ERROR checksum mismatch for shard shard-42.bin expected=9f2c... got=1a7b...

HTTP trace from downloader: GET /presigned/object HTTP/1.1
Host: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Range: bytes=0-4194303

Response: HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Type: multipart/byteranges; boundary=--MIXED_BOUNDARY
Content-Length: 125673

--MIXED_BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Content-Range: bytes 0-2047999/8388608

<binary part A>
--MIXED_BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Content-Range: bytes 2048000-4194303/8388608

<binary part B>
--MIXED_BOUNDARY--
InspectPro appliance logs: 2026-03-09T18:21:12Z CONNECT-peek detected SNI=s3.amazonaws.com -> performed HTTP/3->HTTP/2 downgrade and range-splitting optimization (rule id 4121)
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Customer opened after multiple node restarts; attaching initial logs and presigned URL header traces.
2026-03-10 Support (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed checksum mismatches on a repro cluster provided by BrightFrame. Noted multipart/byteranges responses in traces — unusual for single Range requests.
2026-03-11 BrightFrame (customer): Appliance vendor confirmed rule 4121 will split large range requests into two subranges for streaming inspection; they can modify, but need guidance on safe config.

2026-03-11 Eng (SRE - Maria Gomez): Hypothesis: downloader assumes single-range 206 and writes file sequentially; multipart responses change order/headers and break reassembly. Suggested adding multipart/byteranges handling or checksum validation and retry on multipart response.

2026-03-12 Support (Liam O'Connor): Applied immediate workaround: updated VPCE egress ACL to bypass appliance for s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com from serving subnets. Customer confirmed successful startup of previously failing nodes.
2026-03-12 BrightFrame: Confirmed nodes stabilized after bypass; requesting permanent solution and guidance for other customers behind similar appliances.
investigation_notes: Observed consistent pattern: when appliance rule 4121 is active, presigned GETs containing a single Range are rewritten into two subranges; response becomes multipart/byteranges with boundary-delimited parts.

Redwood artifact downloader (current release) expects a simple 206+single Content-Range or a full 200 body for non-range. It streams response directly into a shard file and does not parse multipart/byteranges boundaries, resulting in mixed binary parts and a bad checksum.

Appliance vendor rationale: splitting large ranges improves inline inspection throughput and avoids large content peek windows for memory-constrained appliances. However this behavior is incompatible with our presigned shard fetch semantics and the downloader's assumptions.
We reproduced locally using InspectPro emulator and validated the multipart response. Confirmed bypassing the appliance restores single-range 206 responses and correct checksums.

Risk assessment: Multiple enterprise customers using inline inspection appliances could be impacted, particularly when their egress appliance has similar 'range split' optimizations and when using VPCE egress paths that route presigned S3 traffic through such appliances.
resolution: Workaround (applied): Customer added an egress bypass rule in VPCE/NGW to allow direct traffic to s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com from serving subnets. Immediate effect: serving nodes restarted and downloaded shards successfully.

Short-term mitigation: Document guidance for support engineers: detect multipart/byteranges in downloader logs and advise customers to add host-level bypass rules or disable 'range-splitting' rule on appliance.

Medium-term fix (planned): Implement multipart/byteranges support in artifact-downloader to correctly parse and reassemble parts when server returns multipart responses, and validate final checksum; add a retry path if multipart detected because of middlebox rewrite.

Long-term prevention: Add an egress-check to Private deployment health-checks that validates presigned URL fetch returns expected single-range 206; surface alert in Console when middlebox rewrite detected and provide one-click bypass suggestions.

Follow-ups: Eng ticket to implement downloader changes and tests created (linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/487). Security to assess whether bypass recommendations require additional guidance for restricted environments.
Status: Workaround accepted by customer; downloader fix targeted for next minor release (ETA 2026-04-02).
